question_text: In an ionic-concentration corrosion cell involving nickel (forming $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ), an electrical current of 5 mA is measured. How many Ni atoms per second are oxidized at the anode? Give your answer as the value of Ni_atoms_per_second.The unit of the answer is s^-1.
response:
The current $I = 5\,\text{mA} = 0.005\,\text{A}$ corresponds to a charge flow of $0.005\,\text{C/s}$. Each Ni atom oxidized to $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ releases 2 electrons, so:

$$\text{Ni atoms/s} = \frac{I}{2e} = \frac{0.005}{2(1.602\times10^{-19})} \approx 1.56\times10^{16}\,\text{s}^{-1}$$

$$\boxed{1.56\times10^{16}}$$
